findings.issue_text: Docs claim the {project_name} Operator will fail when rolling-updates is not enabled, but no operator runtime code implementing that gate exists in this diff, causing doc/behavior divergence

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently renumbered from 4 to 3 with 4 reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking external scripts relying on the existing exit-code contract without deprecation or release notes

Dockerfile-custom-image hardcodes --features=rolling-updates into the test image's persisted config, so operator integration tests silently run with the feature enabled and tests asserting default disabled behavior cannot be written against this image
testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error string and does not assert the exit code equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), leaving the doc-advertised exit-code contract unverified

UpgradeTest.java always sets ROLLING_UPDATES as enabled in createInitialDeployment, so no test exercises the Keycloak CR without rolling-updates to verify the operator actually fails/rejects it as documented

RECREATE_UPGRADE exit code changed from 4 to 3 but no test asserts the recreate exit code (e.g., assertEquals(3, result.exitCode()) in testWrongVersions)
testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error text, not that exitCode == 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED
Exit code 4 is repurposed from RECREATE_UPGRADE to FEATURE_DISABLED, silently breaking automation/CI that parses 4 as 'recreate required' and misclassifying disabled-feature runs as recreate-required
Feature-disabled gating in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() exits before validateConfig(), reordering diagnostics with no test covering metadata subcommand with flag disabled plus missing option
No symmetric test for UpdateCompatibilityCheck with the flag disabled plus missing --input; the check-subcommand disabled path is untested
Dockerfile-custom-image bakes --features=rolling-updates into the custom image while the comparison base image lacks it, potentially causing feature-set incompatibility in the upgrade test
No test asserts whether rolling-updates appearing/disappearing in the feature list affects the compatibility verdict, leaving feature-list differences unverified in compatibility comparison
RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3 with FEATURE_DISABLED reusing 4, breaking external scripts and CI pipelines that branch on exit code 4
Docs claim the Operator will fail if rolling-updates is not enabled, but the diff contains no operator main-code changes enforcing that invariant
Identical feature-gate block duplicated verbatim in UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata instead of being hoisted into the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand base class

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3, breaking the documented exit-code contract relied upon by external scripts, docs, and the operator's update-strategy logic, causing CI pipelines to misinterpret 'recreate required' and 'feature disabled' results

picocli.exit(...) is not a valid call (picocli is a package with no static exit method), potentially breaking the build, and the feature-disabled gate is duplicated inline in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46 and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46 instead of the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand parent, risking drift for future subcommands

The CI stand-in test enables rolling-upgrades via a test-only Dockerfile build-time flag rather than the documented CR spec.features path, so a green UpgradeTest does not verify the CR-declared feature actually enables the check in operator-managed pods

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently renumbered from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult.java, with 4 reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking existing automation/scripts keyed on exit code 4 which will now interpret 'feature disabled' as 'recreate required' and shut down a healthy cluster
Docs add the exit code 4 'feature disabled' row without documenting that the 'recreate required' exit code moved from 4 to 3, leaving contradictory interpretations of exit code 4 in the ecosystem
Docs CAUTION claims the Operator will fail when rolling-updates is not enabled, but no operator-side enforcement appears in the diff, leaving the documented contract unbacked

Baking --features=rolling-updates into operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image silently enables a preview feature for anyone reusing the Dockerfile pattern, with no signal that the flag is a test prerequisite rather than a default
RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 with FEATURE_DISABLED taking 4, which may break operators or automation depending on the old exit code (compatibility concern)

testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and never verifies the exit code, so the new picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) exit code 4 is untested and a regression changing the disabled-path exit code to 1 or 0 would go undetected while breaking the operator's upgrade strategy detection

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was silently changed from 4 to 3, a contract change consumed by the operator's UpdateStrategy, but no test asserts exit code 3 for the recreate path (testWrongVersions checks only the error message, not result.exitCode()), so a refactor flipping it back to 4 would go undetected

createInitialDeployment unconditionally enables ROLLING_UPDATES for every parameterized strategy, so the operator's documented failure path when the feature is not enabled is exercised by zero tests in the diff

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 in the same release that introduces FEATURE_DISABLED = 4, silently flipping the meaning of exit code 4 for existing automation (Operator update-strategy probe, CI pipelines, admin scripts) with no transition or documentation

Feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata runs before validateConfig(), so `update-compatibility save-metadata --features=rolling-updates` exits 4 instead of producing metadata when the feature isn't enabled in the persistent build, breaking metadata save on old-version pods during rolling upgrades

Exit code 4 is silently repurposed from 'recreate upgrade required' to 'feature disabled', with no migration signal for external consumers; scripts checking exit code 4 will misclassify a disabled-feature stop as 'recreate upgrade needed' and could shut down a production deployment. No deprecation notice, changelog entry, or distinct exit code (e.g., 5) disambiguates the new semantic.

The feature gate runs before validateConfig() in UpdateCompatibilityCheck, so a user with both an invalid configuration and a disabled feature only learns about the feature problem on first run and hits a different failure on the next run, making the first run's diagnostics misleadingly incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Docs claim the {project_name} Operator will fail when rolling-updates is not enabled, but no operator runtime code implementing that gate exists in this diff, causing doc/behavior divergence

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds docs warnings stating the Operator will fail unless preview feature `rolling-updates` is enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc), but the only Operator-side Java change shown is in a test (UpgradeTest) to set the feature in the CR; there is no corresponding Operator runtime/controller logic in this diff that enforces or detects this condition. The diff *does* add gating for the CLI update-compatibility commands (Profile.isFeatureEnabled + FEATURE_DISABLED exit code), but not for the Operator, so the new Operator doc claim is not backed by code visible in this PR diff, creating a likely doc/behavior divergence or missing implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently renumbered from 4 to 3 with 4 reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking external scripts relying on the existing exit-code contract without deprecation or release notes

Dockerfile-custom-image hardcodes --features=rolling-updates into the test image's persisted config, so operator integration tests silently run with the feature enabled and tests asserting default disabled behavior cannot be written against this image

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` now runs `kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`, so the feature is hardcoded into that custom image build. However, the finding’s broader claim—that operator integration tests use this image and therefore “silently run with the feature enabled” such that default-disabled behavior can’t be tested—cannot be verified from the diff: no test or harness code here references this Dockerfile, and tests shown either explicitly enable the feature via CLI args (`ENABLE_FEATURE`) or via CR `FeatureSpec` (`UpgradeTest`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error string and does not assert the exit code equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), leaving the doc-advertised exit-code contract unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled`, the test only calls `cliResult.assertError("Unable to use this command...")` and does not assert the process exit code. The diff introduces an explicit exit code contract for this case (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and the commands call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled, plus the docs add a new result row `m|4` for the disabled-feature case. That behavior is not currently verified by the test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UpgradeTest.java always sets ROLLING_UPDATES as enabled in createInitialDeployment, so no test exercises the Keycloak CR without rolling-updates to verify the operator actually fails/rejects it as documented

adjudication.rationale: In `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment`, the PR now unconditionally enables the preview feature by doing `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()));`. That means these operator integration tests no longer cover (and never assert) the documented failure path when `rolling-updates` is not enabled in the Keycloak CR. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap around newly documented behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The operator-side enforcement of the documented 'fails when rolling-updates is disabled' behavior has no implementation in the diff and no test guarding it

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds documentation warnings that the Keycloak Operator will fail if the preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc), but the only operator-side code change shown is in a test helper (UpgradeTest.java) that unconditionally enables the feature via `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(...)`. There is no operator runtime/controller logic in this diff that enforces or checks for `rolling-updates` being enabled, and there is no operator test that asserts failure/behavior when the feature is disabled. (The enforcement added in this diff is for CLI commands, not the operator.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE exit code changed from 4 to 3 but no test asserts the recreate exit code (e.g., assertEquals(3, result.exitCode()) in testWrongVersions)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (in `CompatibilityResult.java`). In `UpdateCommandDistTest.testWrongVersions`, the tests only assert the error text (e.g., `result.assertError(...)`) and never assert the process exit code for the recreate/incompatible cases, so the changed exit-code contract is not covered by tests as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error text, not that exitCode == 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new failure mode and exit code: both UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata call picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) when Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES is disabled, and CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED is defined as 4. However, the new testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest only asserts the error message and does not assert that the process exits with code 4, so the new exit-code behavior is unverified by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exit code 4 is repurposed from RECREATE_UPGRADE to FEATURE_DISABLED, silently breaking automation/CI that parses 4 as 'recreate required' and misclassifying disabled-feature runs as recreate-required

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (see `CompatibilityResult.java`). That repurposes exit code 4 from “recreate required” to “feature disabled”, which is a backward-incompatible behavioral change for any external automation relying on the previous meaning of exit code 4. The claim about CI/automation breakage is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-disabled gating in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() exits before validateConfig(), reordering diagnostics with no test covering metadata subcommand with flag disabled plus missing option

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` (and `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()`), the new feature gate `if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) { ... return; }` is placed before `printPreviewWarning(); validateConfig();` (see added block in both classes). This does change diagnostic precedence: when the feature is disabled, config/option validation errors won’t be reported because the command exits first. The added dist test `testFeatureNotEnabled` covers the feature-disabled message for `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata`, but there is no test exercising how metadata/check behave when both the feature is disabled and required/invalid options are present (e.g., for `check` missing `--input`). This is a specific, diff-grounded UX/testing gap rather than a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No symmetric test for UpdateCompatibilityCheck with the flag disabled plus missing --input; the check-subcommand disabled path is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an early feature-gate in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` that exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` before option validation. The new dist test `testFeatureNotEnabled` only launches `{UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME}` without `--features=rolling-updates`, so the disabled path is covered for Metadata but not for Check. Meanwhile, `testMissingOptionOnCheck` now always passes `ENABLE_FEATURE`, so there is no test that `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` with the feature disabled (and missing `--input`) hits the feature-disabled branch instead of the "Missing required argument" path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dockerfile-custom-image bakes --features=rolling-updates into the custom image while the comparison base image lacks it, potentially causing feature-set incompatibility in the upgrade test

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` adding `--features=rolling-updates` to `kc.sh build`, but nothing in the shown changes indicates this Dockerfile is used by the upgrade test or compared against a “base image” lacking that flag. In fact, the operator integration `UpgradeTest` was updated to explicitly enable the `rolling-updates` feature in the CR (`setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`), and the CLI commands now explicitly fail if the feature is not enabled. The claimed “feature-set incompatibility in the upgrade test” is therefore not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test asserts whether rolling-updates appearing/disappearing in the feature list affects the compatibility verdict, leaving feature-list differences unverified in compatibility comparison

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not introduce or show any compatibility comparison logic based on a “feature list” changing; it only adds a new preview feature key (Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES) and gates the update-compatibility commands to fail fast when that feature is not enabled (UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata calling Profile.isFeatureEnabled and exiting with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED). The added dist test explicitly covers the disabled-feature case (testFeatureNotEnabled) and enables the feature for other compatibility tests via --features=rolling-updates. There’s nothing in the shown diff to verify a missing test about feature-list differences affecting the compatibility verdict.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3 with FEATURE_DISABLED reusing 4, breaking external scripts and CI pipelines that branch on exit code 4

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (`CompatibilityResult.java`). That is a backward-incompatible change in the CLI exit-code contract and is not called out elsewhere in the diff; external automation branching on exit code `4` for “recreate upgrade” would now misinterpret it as “feature disabled.” This is a real compatibility concern grounded in the diff, though it may be intentional rather than a correctness bug in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Docs claim the Operator will fail if rolling-updates is not enabled, but the diff contains no operator main-code changes enforcing that invariant

adjudication.rationale: The docs add a CAUTION in `docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc` stating the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled, but the diff shows no corresponding Operator runtime/main-code change to enforce or trigger this behavior (only a test change in `operator/.../UpgradeTest.java` that enables the feature, plus CLI-side enforcement in Quarkus commands). Whether the Operator already fails without the feature can’t be verified from this diff, so this is a doc/code-consistency/scope concern rather than a confirmed functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Identical feature-gate block duplicated verbatim in UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata instead of being hoisted into the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand base class

adjudication.rationale:
The diff shows the same feature-gate logic added verbatim to both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`:
`if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) { printFeatureDisabled(); picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED); return; }`.
`AbstractUpdatesCommand` only gains `printFeatureDisabled()` but does not centralize the gating itself, so the reviewer’s point about duplication (and potential to hoist into the shared base) is accurate. This is a maintainability/architecture concern, not a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3, breaking the documented exit-code contract relied upon by external scripts, docs, and the operator's update-strategy logic, causing CI pipelines to misinterpret 'recreate required' and 'feature disabled' results

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* change `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (quarkus/runtime/.../CompatibilityResult.java). That is a concrete, externally observable behavioral change that could break any external automation relying on the previous numeric exit code. However, the claim that this breaks a *documented* contract and the operator’s update-strategy logic (and thus CI pipelines) is not verifiable from the diff alone (no operator logic shown; docs appear to be updated to include code 4 for “feature disabled”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: picocli.exit(...) is not a valid call (picocli is a package with no static exit method), potentially breaking the build, and the feature-disabled gate is duplicated inline in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46 and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46 instead of the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand parent, risking drift for future subcommands

adjudication.rationale: In both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`, the diff adds `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);`. The only picocli-related import shown is `import picocli.CommandLine;` and `picocli` is used as a lowercase identifier, which in Java would be interpreted as a package name, not a type. You cannot call a static method on a package, so this is a compile-time error unless some unrelated class named `picocli` exists (not evidenced in the diff). The duplication note is accurate (the feature gate is repeated in both classes even though `AbstractUpdatesCommand` now contains `printFeatureDisabled()`), but the invalid `picocli.exit(...)` call is a concrete, build-breaking defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The CI stand-in test enables rolling-upgrades via a test-only Dockerfile build-time flag rather than the documented CR spec.features path, so a green UpgradeTest does not verify the CR-declared feature actually enables the check in operator-managed pods

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the operator integration `UpgradeTest` was updated to enable the feature through the CR spec path: it creates/initializes `FeatureSpec` and calls `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`. That directly exercises `spec.features.enabled` semantics, not a Dockerfile build-time flag. While `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` also adds `--features=rolling-updates`, the finding’s claim that the CI stand-in/UpgradeTest relies on that instead of the CR feature spec is not supported by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (CompatibilityResult.java). That is a backward-incompatible behavior change for any external automation keyed on the old exit code value, and the change is not mitigated in code (only a comment and new behavior). The specific “shut down a healthy cluster” consequence is speculative, but the exit-code renumbering/breakage concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Docs add the exit code 4 'feature disabled' row without documenting that the 'recreate required' exit code moved from 4 to 3, leaving contradictory interpretations of exit code 4 in the ecosystem

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changed from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`. In `update-compatibility.adoc`, the existing row `m|3` describes “Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The deployment must be shut down…”, which aligns with “recreate required”, and the new `m|4` row is explicitly “The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.” There is no contradictory interpretation of exit code 4 within the diff; 4 is consistently used for “feature disabled” after the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Docs CAUTION claims the Operator will fail when rolling-updates is not enabled, but no operator-side enforcement appears in the diff, leaving the documented contract unbacked

adjudication.rationale: The operator docs add a CAUTION saying the Operator will fail unless preview feature `rolling-updates` is enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc), but the diff only shows operator-side tests and a custom image Dockerfile enabling the feature (UpgradeTest.java, Dockerfile-custom-image). There is no operator runtime/controller logic in the diff that enforces/validates this requirement or fails fast when the feature is disabled, so the documented guarantee isn’t backed by any new operator-side enforcement shown here (even though it might already fail for other reasons outside the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Baking --features=rolling-updates into operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image silently enables a preview feature for anyone reusing the Dockerfile pattern, with no signal that the flag is a test prerequisite rather than a default

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` to always run `kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`, which does unconditionally enable a preview feature in any image built from this example Dockerfile. The Dockerfile itself contains no comment explaining this is required while the feature is in preview; that rationale only appears in docs elsewhere (`advanced-configuration.adoc`, `update-compatibility.adoc`). This is a concrete review concern about surprising defaults/documentation placement rather than a demonstrable correctness bug in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 with FEATURE_DISABLED taking 4, which may break operators or automation depending on the old exit code (compatibility concern)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (see `quarkus/runtime/.../CompatibilityResult.java`). That is an intentional behavioral/contract change that could break external automation relying on the previous exit code mapping. The diff doesn’t show any internal defect, but it does create a compatibility concern that may need explicit communication (e.g., release notes / migration guidance).

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and never verifies the exit code, so the new picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) exit code 4 is untested and a regression changing the disabled-path exit code to 1 or 0 would go undetected while breaking the operator's upgrade strategy detection

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only calls `cliResult.assertError(...)` and does not assert the process exit code. The production code in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` / `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` now explicitly calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is disabled, and `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` is defined as `4`. Because the test doesn’t verify `exitCode() == 4`, a regression changing that disabled-path exit code could slip by while the error text remains the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was silently changed from 4 to 3, a contract change consumed by the operator's UpdateStrategy, but no test asserts exit code 3 for the recreate path (testWrongVersions checks only the error message, not result.exitCode()), so a refactor flipping it back to 4 would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` (`CompatibilityResult.java`), which is a behavioral/contract change for CLI exit codes. In the integration test `UpdateCommandDistTest#testWrongVersions`, the recreate/incompatible path asserts only the error text and does not assert `result.exitCode()`, so an accidental change of the recreate exit code (e.g., back to 4) would not be caught by these tests. The diff does not show an immediate functional break, but it does introduce an untested contract change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: createInitialDeployment unconditionally enables ROLLING_UPDATES for every parameterized strategy, so the operator's documented failure path when the feature is not enabled is exercised by zero tests in the diff

adjudication.rationale: In `operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java`, `createInitialDeployment(UpdateStrategy updateStrategy)` now always initializes `FeatureSpec` and unconditionally enables `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` via `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`. Because this helper is used to create the initial deployment for each parameterized `UpdateStrategy`, the operator integration tests added/modified here cannot exercise any “feature disabled”/failure behavior for the operator when `rolling-updates` is not enabled. While the diff does add a CLI test for the disabled-feature path (`testFeatureNotEnabled` in `UpdateCommandDistTest`), no operator-side test in this diff covers the documented/operator failure scenario when the feature is off.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 in the same release that introduces FEATURE_DISABLED = 4, silently flipping the meaning of exit code 4 for existing automation (Operator update-strategy probe, CI pipelines, admin scripts) with no transition or documentation

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (in `quarkus/runtime/.../CompatibilityResult.java`). That does flip the meaning of exit code 4 for callers that previously interpreted 4 as “recreate upgrade required”. The diff also updates docs to mention code 4 as feature-disabled, but it does not show any transition/compat handling for existing consumers. This is a real, diff-grounded backward-compatibility concern rather than an internal correctness bug proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The feature gate runs before validateConfig() in UpdateCompatibilityCheck, so a user with both an invalid configuration and a disabled feature only learns about the feature problem on first run and hits a different failure on the next run, making the first run's diagnostics misleadingly incomplete.

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`), the diff adds an early return when `!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` before `validateConfig()`. That means if both the feature is disabled and the config is invalid, the user will only see the feature-disabled error on the first run and only see config validation errors after enabling the feature. This is a real, diff-grounded diagnostic/UX concern, but not a functional defect since the docs explicitly say the command/operator will fail unless the preview feature is enabled and the early exit is intentional.
